chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-ʿAlawī, from al-ʿAmrakī, from ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man in janabah, or without wudu (ablution), who has no water with him, but he comes upon snow and earth: which of the two is better? Should he perform tayammum, or wipe his face with the snow? He said: “Snow is better if it moistens his head and body; but if he is unable to perform ghusl with it, then let him perform tayammum.”

Then he said—may Allah the Exalted support him—if he is in a land of rock or stones upon which there is no dust, he should also place his hands upon them and wipe his face and his palms just as we mentioned regarding his tayammum with dust. There is no hardship upon him in praying with that due to the circumstance of necessity, and no repetition is required of him.

The aspect of indication for this is that these stones are referred to by the name of earth, and when that designation is applied to them, they fall under the apparent meaning that has already been mentioned.

Then he said—may Allah the Exalted support him—whenever the one performing tayammum finds water and is able to use it, and does not fear for himself from purification with it, the prayer is not sufficient for him until he purifies himself with it. But for what he had prayed with tayammum, there is no making up required upon him.

(555) 29. What indicates this is what al-Shaykh—may Allah the Exalted support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from one of the two عليهما السلام, who said:

“When the traveler does not find water, then let him seek it so long as there is still time. فإذا he fears that the time will pass him by, then let him perform tayammum and pray at the end of the time. Then, if he finds water, there is no making up required of him, and let him perform wudu (ablution) for what lies ahead.”

key_terms.الِاضْطِرَارِ: a state of necessity that affects legal ruling
key_terms.الْجُنُبِ: a person in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.ثَلْجًا: snow used here as a possible means of purification
key_terms.صَعِيدًا: earth or ground used for tayammum
key_terms.قَضَاءٌ: making up a prayer after its time
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat
key_terms.يَتَيَمَّمْ: to perform tayammum as dry ablution

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about tayammum with snow or stone when water is unavailable?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the rulings of tayammum for one in janabah or without wudu (ablution) when water is unavailable, especially in situations involving snow, earth, or stone. It establishes that using snow for purification is preferable when possible, that tayammum on stone is valid in necessity, and that prayers already performed with valid tayammum do not require qada' when water is later found.
